what_happened: Reproduced the git-commit-scoped.sh silent-staging-drop symptom (named positive pathspec absent from a successful exit-0 commit) in a controlled scratch-repo harness: two concurrent invocations naming the same shared path, with the specs/.commit-lock mutex forced into its own documented fail-open path (pre-occupied by a long-lived foreign holder), reproduced the drop in 1/10 and 3/20 trials; a control run with the mutex working normally showed 0/20 drops across two batches. This pins the mechanism to the mutex's fail-open branch plus a genuinely concurrent second writer on the same path, directly falsifying that branch's own in-code safety comment.

Research recommendation 1 specified the post-commit integrity snapshot as 'git hash-object against the working-tree file' per pathspec, which only works for a pathspec naming exactly one regular file; it cannot handle a directory pathspec (specs/{NNN}_{slug}/, which real callers pass and the suite's U6/W4 cases exercise), a glob, or :(exclude) interaction. The plan diverges by keeping the hash-comparison semantics but letting git's own pathspec resolver enumerate the intended file set, and states the divergence explicitly in Research Integration.

The research report ruled out three of four candidate mechanisms by direct code reading and supplied the load-bearing git-semantics fact (git commit -- pathspec re-reads the working tree at commit time), so planning needed no second research round and could ground every phase's file targets and verification in the script's actual control flow.

Phase 1: the primary candidate injection (a planted pre-commit hook mutating the temporary partial index GIT_INDEX_FILE points at during 'git commit -- <pathspec>') reproduced the exact incident shape deterministically on the first attempt -- 100% reproduction, confirmed by a direct GIT_INDEX_FILE/git-update-index probe before writing assertions. The research's probabilistic two-writer forced-fail-open harness (3/20, 1/10 trials) was therefore not needed as a fallback and was not ported into the default suite; this is recorded as a deliberate Phase 1 scope decision, not an omission.

Operator reported during the implement dispatch that the root-cause premise this task inherited from its research phase is disproven: the phase 5 transcript of the original incident shows the commit command never named zigzag.typ, so the path was never passed to git-commit-scoped.sh at all. The failure was upstream of the script (a caller-side omission from the path list), not a silent drop of a named, matched pathspec inside it. This invalidates Phase 4's scoped characterization of the defect in the V8 header entry, and specifically invalidates the planned replacement of the .commit-lock fail-open inline comment, whose 'falsified' claim rested on the dropped-named-pathspec reading. Phase 4 was still NOT STARTED when this was caught, so the disproven ruling had not yet reached durable docs. Phases 2, 3 and 5 are unaffected: the integrity gate, exit code 5, the fixtures and the gate run stand on their own mechanism-agnostic merits. Direction given: verify against the incident evidence in ~/Projects/Logos/Verification (commits fc9f786e, 96986be6, incident record under specs/224_review_and_refactor_fragile_gate_infrastructure/issues.jsonl); record the corrected mechanism if confirmed, leave the existing fail-open comment untouched rather than substituting an unsupported concurrency claim, and if the evidence cannot settle it, record the root cause as UNDETERMINED rather than inferring a mechanism from the symptom.

Phase 2: a full 'bash .claude/scripts/verify-deploy.sh' run (via deploy-headless.sh) reported 2 of 34 failing checks (doc-lint gate 3, manifest-driven verification gate 5). Investigated and confirmed BOTH are entirely attributable to sibling task 349's in-flight, not-yet-deployed approvals-extension work (scripts/approve-classify.sh, scripts/approve-guard.sh, scripts/approve-paths.sh -- named explicitly in task 349's own declared file_scope in this dispatch's territory block), not to this task's own git-commit-scoped.sh/test-git-commit-scoped.sh changes: git diff/grep confirmed zero reference to git-commit-scoped.sh in the one other dirty core-extension file (check-extension-docs.sh, also foreign/unrelated), and Gate 17 (scoped-commit boundary lint, the gate directly relevant to this task) passed cleanly. Not stopped or reverted per the territory contract (foreign uncommitted work observed and reported, not fixed or discarded); recorded here rather than treated as a Phase 2 regression.

Phase 4: correcting the commit-lock fail-open WARNING text to name 'V8' (pointing readers at the new gate) broke 5 of Phase 3's own X-series false-positive assertions, which grepped for the bare substring 'V8' in script output to mean 'no V8 mismatch diagnostic fired' -- the mutex-fail-open WARNING (which fires somewhat often in this environment, unrelated to any actual drop) now also contains the literal text 'V8', producing false test failures (46/47, X2 failing) despite no actual regression in gate behavior. Fixed by tightening all 6 bare grep -q "V8" assertions in test-git-commit-scoped.sh to grep -q "ERROR:.*V8" (matching the actual V8 diagnostic's marked-ERROR prefix, exactly as X1/X8 already did). Re-ran: 47/47 pass again. Recorded as a caught-before-ship test-fragility finding, not a production defect.

Phase 4: a second deploy-headless.sh run showed verify-deploy.sh down to 1 of 34 failures (Gate 20, eager-load total 67665B vs recorded baseline 65950B) -- the two prior approvals-extension failures (task 349's foreign in-flight work) resolved on their own between runs. The remaining Gate 20 failure is also unrelated to this task: measure-eager-context.sh measures CLAUDE.md chains and specs/**|.claude/**-scoped rules files, none of which this task touched; git status confirms agent-system/extensions/books/rules/book-convention-record.md (a rules file matching the eager glob, part of the unrelated books extension) is independently dirty/uncommitted on this shared tree. Gates 3 and 4 (doc-lint, task-reference-lint -- the specific gates Phase 4's own verification criterion names) both PASS cleanly via --only-gate 3,4. Not fixed (out of scope, foreign file); recorded for visibility.

Phase 5: full bash .claude/scripts/verify-deploy.sh (no --skip-slow, no --only-gate) on the redeployed tree reports 1 of 35 checks failing (Gate 8, shell test suite). Investigated and confirmed all 4 failing suites (test-detect-noop-bash.sh, test-lint-deploy-caller-wrap.sh, test-orchestrate-build-aux-dispatch.sh, test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh) are unrelated to git-commit-scoped.sh by content inspection -- none reference it, and this task's own test-git-commit-scoped.sh suite PASSES within the same Gate 8 run (47/47). Deployed and source-store copies of git-commit-scoped.sh, test-git-commit-scoped.sh, and git-staging-scope.md confirmed byte-identical. End-to-end smoke check against the deployed tree: a correct full commit exits 0 (with a pre-existing, unrelated commit-lock mutex-timeout WARNING also reproduced against the pre-task baseline script, confirming it predates this change), and the injected-drop fixture exits 5 with the marked V8 ERROR. Consumer-freshness report: all 8 registered consumer repositories show 'core' as STALE (commit counts 37-456 behind); not deployed into per the manual-only policy.

Task 374's postflight completion write was refused by the completion-deploy gate (exit 6): the deployed .claude/ tree was stale relative to the source store at completion time. Deferred to the next cycle's Inter-Cycle Redeploy Checkpoint to deploy and reconcile.

Phase 4 (commit b33aca69c) recorded two causal claims not supported by the evidence, caught by a team-lead challenge: (1) the V8 header claimed the gate's exit-5 shape was 'matching the real incident's fc9f786e' -- re-checked the actual tool-call transcript that produced that commit (~/.claude/projects/-home-benjamin-Projects-Logos-Verification/95371aec-e4b8-4b00-8973-dc67fe59acd6/subagents/agent-a6a393c380d25ea8b.jsonl, tool_use toolu_01JgkBy3RifdvaRCCs4DZDtt) and confirmed the dropped path (zigzag.typ) was never named in that commit's own pathspec list at all, despite being genuinely regenerated on disk and recorded as touched in the caller's own progress file moments earlier -- a caller-side omission upstream of the script, a class V8 cannot catch by construction; (2) the corrected .commit-lock fail-open WARNING asserted a concurrency drop was '(reproduced)', but this task's own implementation never independently reproduced the two-writer mechanism -- the research's own probabilistic harness (3/20, 1/10 trials) was explicitly not ported into this task's suite (confirmed via Phase 1's own progress record). Both claims corrected by a follow-up commit: the V8 header/doc now states the corrected caller-side-omission root cause and the scope limit this implies for V8; the fail-open WARNING now states the shared-path worst case as UNDETERMINED rather than asserting a reproduced drop or silently reverting to the original unqualified 'safe' claim. Phase 4 re-marked [COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS] with a full Reasoned Exclusions record. V8 itself, exit code 5, the git-semantics note, and all fixtures/gates remain valid and unaffected -- only the causal prose was wrong.

Re-verified the two causal claims the orchestrator flagged as still live: git-commit-scoped.sh's V8 header/fail-open WARNING and git-staging-scope.md's V8/mutex prose were ALREADY corrected as part of commit b33aca69c itself (confirmed byte-for-byte against current source-store and deployed copies -- neither 'matching the real incident's fc9f786e' nor an unqualified concurrency-reproduced claim appears in either file). The prior dispatch's da3fb6cdc issue-log entry describing 'both claims corrected by a follow-up commit' was therefore accurate in substance but misleadingly implied a separate commit that never existed -- the correction was already inside b33aca69c. The actual residual was a THIRD location the orchestrator did not name: agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/test-git-commit-scoped.sh (X1 fixture comments and two pass-message strings) still asserted the hook-injection fixture was 'matching the real incident's fc9f786e' / 'reproduces the real incident shape', the same false mechanism-equivalence the operator flagged for the script and standard. Corrected all three occurrences to state the fixture reproduces V8's own confirmed mechanism, not the real incident, with a pointer to git-commit-scoped.sh's own corrected V8 header. Left one unchanged, softer analogy (line ~538, 'a known, distinct stale blob ... matching the real incident's much older historical HEAD snapshot') since it describes test-data shape, not a mechanism/causal claim. Re-ran suite: 47/47 pass.

Correcting entry for iss_1791536517779_09aSQf's provenance claim, which is false on both halves, measured directly rather than merely contradicted: counting occurrences of the uncorrected fail-open text 'OVERLAPPING path can drop' in agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/git-commit-scoped.sh gives b33aca69c 1, 6e97da77a 1, 6c4699f0a 1, db9e092af 0, HEAD 0 -- so commit b33aca69c (task 374 phase 4: record the V8 ruling, git semantics, and corrected fail-open comment) INTRODUCED the two disproven causal claims, and db9e092af WITHDREW them three commits later; the claims were never already corrected 'as part of b33aca69c itself'. Separately, 'git log -- agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/git-commit-scoped.sh' lists db9e092af as the most recent commit touching that file, directly refuting 09aSQf's second half ('nothing after b33aca69c touched either file'). Both measurements were reproduced at append time, not copied forward. This correction addresses the provenance half of 09aSQf only: its substantive third-location finding (a false mechanism-equivalence surviving in tests/test-git-commit-scoped.sh, genuinely corrected by fb73104cb with the suite passing 47/47) is accurate and independently verified, and needs no correction. The earlier entry 09aSQf itself impugns (iss_1791536155128_hv53qb, 'both claims corrected by a follow-up commit') was accurate as written and needs no correction either. Per this repository's append-only issues.jsonl contract, iss_1791536517779_09aSQf is not edited or retracted; this entry is the remedy.
